subject: Next steps: Procurement & commercial path for Redwood pilot
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: Procurement & commercial path for Redwood pilot

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really constructive call. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Pilot scope: 2 models, up to 100k inference tokens/day during the pilot (as discussed).
- Technical items: we'll share the sandbox credentials and minimal onboarding checklist; Neha will own the technical kickoff.
- Procurement / commercial: a few items we need to confirm from your side so procurement can move quickly:
  - Preferred payment method: PO (billing via AP) vs corporate card?
  - Vendor onboarding: do you require a W-9 / vendor setup form?
  - Contracting path: do you prefer a redwood MSA + SOW, or purchase via AWS Marketplace?
  - Budget owner and signatory: who in finance owns approvals and who signs?

I've attached our procurement questionnaire, a blank SOW template, and the pricing sheet to speed review. Can you confirm the path you prefer and share the vendor setup contact?

Proposed next step: if a PO/vendor setup is required, would it be possible to get a 30-minute finance intro next week (suggest Tue 17 Mar 10:00am PT)? If Marketplace is preferred we can share marketplace listing timelines but it typically adds a few weeks.

Attachments: [procurement_questionnaire.pdf] [SOW-template.docx] [redwood-pricing-sheet.xlsx]

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0189

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: Procurement & commercial path for Redwood pilot

Marissa — thanks for the follow-up and the materials. Quick answers from procurement: 

- Payment method: we generally do PO for vendors; card is only for smaller SaaS. PO is preferred.
- Vendor onboarding: yes, procurement will need a W-9 and vendor registration. They will also ask for our internal vendor questionnaire; happy to share what they need.
- Marketplace: AWS Marketplace would be ideal for long-term procurement but that process can add ~3-6 weeks. For the pilot, PO is the faster route.
- Budget owner: Priya Singh (VP Product) is the buyer for this initiative.
- Signatory: CFO Martin Hale signs larger vendor contracts (martin.hale@acme.com).

A couple of questions for you: do you accept Net30 payment terms? Also, can you provide a copy of your SOC2 report and the standard MSA (so our legal can start redlines)?

If you can get the vendor packet + SOC2 over, procurement will start the vendor set-up while we align internally on signatories.

— Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Partnerships | Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 17:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: Procurement & commercial path for Redwood pilot

Alex — great, thanks for the clarity. Quick answers and proposed plan: 

- Net30: we can support Net30 on Dedicated/reserved contracts after a standard credit check. For Hosted consumption accounts we typically require card-on-file, but we can make an exception for enterprise pilots if procurement completes vendor setup and agrees to invoiced terms.
- SOC2 / security: here's a link to our SOC2 report and vendor security packet: https://redwood.security/soc2-report (I've also attached the vendor packet).
- MSA / redlines: attaching our standard MSA and SOW template (SOW-template.docx). If it helps, we can provide a redlined starter to accelerate legal review.

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll send the vendor onboarding packet and procurement_questionnaire (attached) — please fill what you can and send to your procurement contact.
2) Let's set a 30-min intro between your procurement/finance and our finance ops to align on payment terms and vendor setup. Proposed slot: Wed, 17 Mar 10:00am PT — does that work for Priya / Alex?
3) Vivek will follow-up internally on pricing structure and any required exceptions for committed Dedicated capacity.

Quoting your note below for context: 

> On Thu, 12 Mar 2026 at 16:02, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com> wrote:
> Alex — thanks for the follow-up and the materials. Quick answers from procurement:
> - Payment method: we generally do PO for vendors; card is only for smaller SaaS. PO is preferred.
> - Vendor onboarding: yes, procurement will need a W-9 and vendor registration.

Attached: [procurement_questionnaire.pdf] [SOW-template.docx] [redwood-pricing-sheet.xlsx]

Neha — can you take point on the technical kickoff tasks once procurement confirms timeline? Priya / Alex — if you share the procurement contact (name/email) I will loop them into the vendor packet.

Best,
Marissa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: Procurement & commercial path for Redwood pilot

Thanks Marissa — I'll join the finance/procurement intro and bring the pricing exception details. My recommendation is we propose a 12-month committed Dedicated option with Net30 invoicing to align with Acme's PO preference and keep unit economics intact. I'll draft a starter SOW and circulate before the call.

-Vivek
